data.name: Victorine
data.gender_notes: Victorine is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Latin victor, meaning ‘conqueror’ or ‘victor.’ The feminine form of Victor, Victorine, signifies a woman who has conquered or a victorious woman. The name Victorine carries the meaning “Conquers the people” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Victorine usually hope their child will grow to embody conquers the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Victorine belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Conquers the people.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Victorine total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Victorine was a popular name for French girls in the 19th and early 20th centuries. It was given to children born during times of adversity, struggles or famine, expressing hope that the child would bring victory and prosperity to their family.
data.spiritual_significance: Victorine reflects the belief in God's divine intervention and the power of faith to overcome challenges. It serves as a reminder that, no matter the circumstances, God is with us and helps us conquer our hardships. This name inspires strength, perseverance, and the pursuit of success in all aspects of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Victorine: Victor's little one. A name meaning triumph and victory for a girl, embodying the strength and courage of the victorious Christ.

historical_references.reference: Victorine de Thebes was a Christian saint who lived during the 3rd century AD. She is believed to have been a young virgin who was martyred during the persecution of Christians by the Roman Emperor Maximian Hercules. According to legend, she was subjected to various tortures, including being exposed to the elements and having her body scraped with iron hooks. Despite her suffering, she remained steadfast in her faith and was eventually beheaded. Her feast day is celebrated on October 7.

Victorine Rasoanaana was a Malagasy queen who ruled the Kingdom of Imerina from 1810 to 1812. She is known for her role in the consolidation of the kingdom and the expansion of its territory. Her reign was marked by military campaigns against neighboring kingdoms and the establishment of a centralized administration. However, her rule was cut short when she was assassinated by a group of nobles who saw her as a threat to their power.
